collection_metadata.locality: Pitchandikulam Forest, Auroville, Tamil Nadu, India

stem_bark.text: The bark of Hardwickia binata is grey brownish-coloured, rough, longitudinally fissured and transversally cracked.
stem_bark.text_html: The bark of Hardwickia binata is grey brownish-coloured, rough, longitudinally fissured and transversally cracked.

seed.text: The seeds of Hardwickia binata are ovate, light brown-coloured and 1.5-2 cm long and 0.7-1 cm wide. There is only one seed per pod.
seed.text_html: The seeds of Hardwickia binata are ovate, light brown-coloured and 1.5-2 cm long and 0.7-1 cm wide. There is only one seed per pod.

fruit.text: The fruit of Hardwickia binata is a samaroid pod . It is flattened, winged, 7-8 cm long and 1.5-1.7 cm wide and brown-coloured. Each pod contains 1 seed.
fruit.text_html: The fruit of Hardwickia binata is a samaroid pod. It is flattened, winged, 7-8 cm long and 1.5-1.7 cm wide and brown-coloured. Each pod contains 1 seed.

leaf.text: The leaves of Hardwickia binata grow alternately on the stem (spirally arranged). The leaf is compound, bifoliate with a 1.5-2 cm petiole. The leaflets are coriaceous and glabrous on both sides (some minute hairs on the margins and on the midrib beneath). The leaflets are sessile. The leaflet of Hardwickia binata is 4-7 cm long and 2.5-4 cm wide. The shape of the blade is ovate-elliptic, the apex is obtuse, the base is obliquely rounded and the margins are entire. The venation of the leaflets is reticulate.
leaf.text_html:
The leaves of Hardwickia binata grow alternately on the stem (spirally arranged).
The leaf is compound, bifoliate with a 1.5-2 cm petiole.
The leaflets are coriaceous and glabrous on both sides (some minute hairs on the margins and on the midrib beneath).
The leaflets are sessile.
The leaflet of Hardwickia binata is 4-7 cm long and 2.5-4 cm wide. The shape of the blade is ovate-elliptic, the apex is obtuse, the base is obliquely rounded and the margins are entire.
The venation of the leaflets is reticulate.

habit.text: Hardwickia binata is a medium-sized and deciduous tree growing up to 20 m high.
habit.text_html: Hardwickia binata is a medium-sized and deciduous tree growing up to 20 m high.

reproduction_dispersal.text_html:
• Sex distribution :
    Hardwickia binata is bisexual (each flower of each individual has both male and female structures).
  • Mode of pollination :
    Hardwickia binata is pollinated by a wide variety of insects.
  • Seed dispersal :
    The winged fruits of Hardwickia binata are dispersed by the wind (anemochory).

phenology.text: ( This phenology applies to southeastern Indian plains )
phenology.text_html:
• Flowering season : From June to December.
  • Fruiting season : From February to June.
  • Seeding season : From February to June.
  • Leaves falling : During the hot season.

    • (This phenology applies to southeastern Indian plains)

veterinary.text: The twigs of Hardwickia binata are used as fodder .
veterinary.text_html: The twigs of Hardwickia binata are used as fodder.

handicrafts.text: The wood of Hardwickia binata is very hard and closed grained. It is used for beams and mine props, bridge and house construction, agricultural implements... The bark yields a strong fibre employed for making ropes. Source : Orwa C., Mutua A., Kindt R., Jamnadass R., Anthony S., 2009, Agroforestree Database: a tree reference and selection guide

reforestation.text_html:
• Planting advice and requirements :
    Hardwickia binata is a light demander and fairly drought resistant. It will grow in a wide variety of situations and soils.
    The species is propagated by seeds or by cuttings.
  • Seed treatments :
    12 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
